thread:
Maya: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-inc) is seeing sudden 429s during short traffic spikes. They say bursts last ~10-30s and then traffic goes back to normal. They pasted this header from a failing request: `x-rw-burst-credits: 0` and `x-rw-rate-limit: 429`. Can SRE confirm if burst credits are being drained too aggressively and whether smoothing can be tuned?

Raj: Looking at logs. I see token-bucket drops to 0 exactly when their spike hits, then a ~15m recover window in metrics (they have small refill_rate). Their requests are pretty parallel — lots of concurrent short lived sessions.

Maya: They claim they didn't change client code — it's likely a PRD load pattern (many users hitting a button). They want guidance: either avoid 429s during spikes or explain how bursting works.

Trevor: Quick explainer for support: we use per-account token-bucket burst credits that let short bursts override sustained rate limits. Capacity = bucket_size; refill_rate = tokens/sec. If they exhaust bucket, requests are throttled (429) until tokens refill. Short spikes can be smoothed by either increasing bucket capacity, increasing refill_rate, or implementing client-side smoothing/backoff.

Raj: Diagnostic data I pulled: `metrics.account.acme-inc.burst_balance` graph shows sharp drop from 800 -> 0 in 12s at 2026-05-02T13:12:10Z, then linear increase ~0.6 tokens/sec. So their configured refill_rate is low (~0.6).

Maya: Is there a way to tune this without enterprise plan? They are on pay-as-you-go.

Lina: short answer: limited options on PAYG. We can offer temporary spike protection (increase burst bucket) as a one-off, or recommend rate-limit smoothing in their client. For Dedicated/Reserved customers we can raise burst profiles per contract.

Maya: Can we give them concrete client-side fixes? We should provide repro steps so they can test.

Trevor: Suggested repro script (can paste into a terminal) to simulate parallel burst against our generation endpoint: 

```bash
# spawn 200 parallel short requests to simulate UI button spam
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rw1-large","input":"short"}' &
done
wait
```

That will likely exhaust a small burst bucket quickly. Use smaller concurrency to test smoothing.

Raj: On the infra side we can recommend these immediate mitigations: 
- Short-term: enable client exponential backoff with jitter and a small local queue (max concurrency per-user). Example: backoff base 200ms, max 2s, jitter 0.5.
- Medium-term: increase refill_rate for this account or bump bucket capacity temporarily (ops change) — requires account team sign-off.
- Long-term: advise moving to Dedicated or raise PAYG burst allotment.

Maya: Any server-side config we can show them in Console so they understand? Something like a smoothing policy?

Trevor: Yes — console exposes three knobs: bucket_capacity, refill_rate, smoothing_window_ms. A sample config we can share (YAML) that operations can apply for customer or they can request via support: 

```yaml
burst_policy:
  bucket_capacity: 1200   # tokens
  refill_rate: 50         # tokens per second
  smoothing_window_ms: 5000  # clients routed through a 5s smoothing window
```

Notes: higher refill_rate reduces duration of throttling; smoothing_window tells our router to spread requests arriving within that window to avoid sudden concurrent bursts hitting model pools. smoothing_window is optional and has latency tradeoffs.

Lina: I'll offer them a temporary bump to bucket_capacity and a one-week monitoring window. Need your sign-off, Raj. Also prep a short blurb Support can send with repro script + recommended client changes.

Raj: +1 to the bump. I'll open a ticket for operations to increase refill_rate to 10 tokens/sec and bucket_capacity to 1000 for one week. Monitoring alert: if 429 rate > 2% for >5m revert or escalate. :eyes:

Maya: Draft message for customer to send now: 

"Thanks — we saw your spike pattern. Short-term we suggest enabling client-side smoothing (exponential backoff + concurrency limit) and we've applied a temporary bump to your burst profile to reduce immediate 429s. To reproduce locally, run the attached shell script to simulate bursts and confirm you see reduced 429s after the bump. For long-term stability consider request queuing or Dedicated capacity"

Trevor: Also add this quick client snippet (JS) showing local concurrency gate + jittered retry: 

```js
// naive concurrency limiter
const MAX_CONC = 8;
let inflight = 0;
const queue = [];
async function send(req) {
  if (inflight >= MAX_CONC) {
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100 + Math.random()*200)); // jitter
    return send(req);
  }
  inflight++;
  try {
    const res = await fetch('/v1/generate', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify(req), headers:{'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}});
    if (res.status === 429) throw new Error('rate_limited');
    return await res.json();
  } finally { inflight--; }
}
```

Maya: Perfect. I'll send the customer the repro script, JS snippet, and let them know we bumped the profile.

ops-bot: Ticket #OPS-8421 opened to increase burst_profile for acme-inc. ETA: 1h for change propagation.

Lina: I'll monitor the account with the customer for the week and collect metrics. If 429s persist after the bump we can propose Dedicated trial.

Maya: Thanks all — closing the loop with customer now. :+1:
